content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Centennial

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma plus five years. Review PMI's exact education and experience thresholds to ensure you qualify before enrolling in Granite PM Academy's bootcamp.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Bootcamp. Attend interactive sessions on your schedule from anywhere, covering all five process groups and ten knowledge areas. Earn your required contact hours through structured, real-world project scenarios led by active certified practitioners.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing bootcamp coursework, submit your formal PMP application directly to PMI. Provide proof of your education, project-management experience, and contact-hour completion. Pay PMI's examination fee to activate your application and secure your exam eligibility.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for Your Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, including practice questions, study guides, and instructor office hours. Schedule your proctored exam with PMI's testing partner. Sit for the 230-question, four-hour exam that assesses your mastery of the PMBOK® Guide and real-world application.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: Earn professional development units (PDUs) throughout your three-year renewal cycle to keep your credential active. Pursue PDUs through training, volunteer work, professional activities, and community engagement. Renew your certification before expiration to continue demonstrating your expertise to your local job market.
